title: Add Redwood Request-ID propagation into template logs + OTel traces (SDK + template conventions)
creator: Monica Patel
content:
## Context
Template apps need to be supportable out of the box. Today, when a user reports an issue, Support/SRE often asks for a Redwood Request ID (from gateway response headers). Template apps currently log trace IDs and some error details, but do not consistently:

1) extract Redwood Request IDs from SDK responses/errors
2) inject them into structured logs
3) attach them to OTel spans as a stable attribute

This creates painful debugging loops (especially for streaming disconnects, 429s, and tool-call failures) because Console-side request logs are keyed primarily by Request ID.

This ticket defines conventions and small SDK/template changes to ensure request IDs propagate reliably in:
- logs (structured, redacted)
- traces (span attributes)
- user-facing error messages (optional, for copy/paste)

## Goals
- Always capture Redwood Request ID (when present) from API responses and failed responses.
- Include it in template structured logs under a consistent field name.
- Attach it to the active span and/or request span in OTel.
- Ensure it works for:
  - normal non-streaming requests
  - streaming requests (including disconnect/reconnect)
  - retries (preserve last-attempt request id; optionally keep all attempt IDs with low-cardinality strategy)

## Non-goals
- Not building a full “request viewer” UX in templates.
- Not adding high-cardinality tags beyond the single request id on spans (and only on relevant spans).
- Not changing gateway behavior; assume the gateway already returns a request ID header.

## Current behavior (observed in templates)
- Python template logs include correlation_id (generated) and trace_id when OTel enabled.
- TS template logs include trace_id, but Request ID is not consistently included.
- In errors, request id is often lost because SDK error types don’t consistently expose headers.

## Proposed conventions
### Field names
- Log field: `redwood.request_id`
- Span attribute: `redwood.request_id`

Rationale: matches Redwood-specific namespace and avoids collision with upstream conventions.

### Extraction rules
- Primary source: HTTP response header from Redwood gateway.
  - Prefer `x-redwood-request-id` (if present)
  - Fallback to `x-request-id` (some proxies normalize)
- For errors:
  - If SDK error includes response headers, extract from there.
  - If connection fails before headers exist, set request_id = "" (do not invent).

### Retry/attempt behavior
- Default: attach only the final attempt’s request_id to the “client request” span.
- Additionally (optional, logs only): if there are multiple attempts, log an array-like string `redwood.request_id_attempts` formatted as comma-separated values (bounded to max 3) to avoid log bloat.
  - Do NOT add attempts list to span attributes (cardinality concern).

### Where to attach
- Templates:
  - On inbound web request span (server span) add request_id when present.
  - For background workers / CLI runs, attach to the root span created by the template for each Redwood API call.
- SDK:
  - Provide helper to surface request id from responses/errors so templates don’t parse headers manually.

## Implementation plan
### 1) SDK changes
Python SDK:
- Add a helper to extract request id from responses and common error types.
- Ensure streaming iterator yields/retains request id on first headers receipt.
- Expose request id on raised exceptions where possible.

TypeScript SDK:
- Add request id to error types and streaming response object.
- Provide a small utility: `getRedwoodRequestId(errOrResponse)`.

Go SDK:
- Align field naming and extraction logic; ensure request id is accessible for middleware/loggers.

### 2) Template changes
- Update request wrapper/middleware to:
  - read request id returned by SDK call
  - set logger context field `redwood.request_id`
  - set active span attribute `redwood.request_id`
- Update troubleshooting docs to instruct users where to find request id in logs.

### 3) Validation
- Unit tests in SDKs for:
  - successful response header extraction
  - error response header extraction (401, 429, 500)
  - streaming: request id present on initial headers even if stream later disconnects
- Template smoke test: a mocked gateway response includes request id; assert it appears in:
  - emitted logs
  - exported span attributes (via test exporter)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For non-streaming calls, template logs contain `redwood.request_id` matching gateway header.
- [ ] For streaming calls, template logs contain `redwood.request_id` even if stream ends early.
- [ ] For failed API calls with a response, the error log includes `redwood.request_id`.
- [ ] OTel traces include `redwood.request_id` on the span that represents the Redwood API call.
- [ ] No additional high-cardinality dimensions are introduced in metrics.

## Notes / constraints
- Observability team requested avoiding request-id on every span; only attach to Redwood API call span and the inbound request span.
- Redaction: request id is not PII; safe to log.
- If user runs behind corporate proxies that strip unknown headers, request id may be unavailable; handle gracefully.

## Links
- Project: Quickstart templates (RAG + agents)
- Related SDK work:
  - redwood-sdk-python PR: `sources/github/redwood-sdk-python/pr-612-add-tracing-context-propagation-helpers.json`
  - redwood-sdk-typescript PR: `sources/github/redwood-sdk-typescript/pr-488-add-streaming-reconnect-and-better-error-types.json` (may need follow-up for request id)
  - redwood-sdk-go PR: `sources/github/redwood-sdk-go/pr-274-add-request-id-extraction-and-logging-fields.json`
- Related template work:
  - Template instrumentation guide: `sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/sdk-guides/sdk-instrumentation-for-quickstarts.json`

## Subtasks
- [ ] Python: add request-id extraction helper + tests (owner: Ibrahim)
- [ ] TS: extend error/response types with request id + tests (owner: Dana)
- [ ] Templates (Py + TS): plumb request id into logger context + span attrs (owner: Sabrina)
- [ ] CI smoke test: validate request id in logs + traces with test exporter (owner: Sahana)

---
## Progress updates
### 2025-02-10 (Monica Patel)
Scoped requirements with Observability. Keep request_id on only the Redwood client span + inbound server span. Avoid adding to metrics dimensions.

### 2025-02-14 (Ibrahim Khan)
Python SDK: prototyped extracting `x-redwood-request-id` from response headers and attaching it to exception object. Need to confirm streaming path: where do we capture headers in the iterator.

### 2025-02-18 (Dana Lo)
TS SDK: found that current error types don’t reliably keep headers for non-2xx responses. Plan: wrap fetch response and propagate headers into a typed `RedwoodError` (w/ `requestId?: string`).

### 2025-02-21 (Allison Grant) — review note
Span naming: attach `redwood.request_id` to span `redwood.llm.request` (or equivalent) and to inbound span only. Don’t attach to tool spans created by the app to avoid over-linking.

### 2025-02-25 (Sabrina James)
Template middleware updated locally to include `redwood.request_id` in logger context. Waiting on SDK surface to avoid manual header parsing in template code.

### 2025-02-27 (Christine Wong) — SRE review
Make sure retries log both attempt count and request id (final). For supportability, include a one-line message on terminal output for CLI flows: “If you contact support, include redwood.request_id=…”.

### 2025-03-01 (Ibrahim Khan)
SDK changes landed behind a small helper API; templates updated to use helper. Tests passing. Requesting review from Monica + Allison. Remaining: TS SDK follow-up PR to ensure headers persist on error responses.

## Review checklist
- [ ] Observability sign-off (Allison)
- [ ] DevEx sign-off (Monica)
- [ ] Template CI smoke test coverage added/updated
- [ ] Docs snippet added to troubleshooting section: “Find your request id”
